scores.name: 物件位置與拖曳生命週期

checks_against.candidate: Scrolling the properties sidebar while a numeric field is focused could still alter Y and move the object to the Scene bottom.
checks_against.result: The root shell captures wheel events; a focused number input is blurred without preventing the same wheel from scrolling its container. X/Y/W/H updates are also constrained to the Scene as a second guard.

checks_against.candidate: A pointer release outside the SVG or a browser interruption could leave dragRef active and apply a stale delta later.
checks_against.result: Window-capture pointerup finalizes the drag, while pointercancel, window blur and hidden visibility cancel the preview and clear drag, pan and guide state.

evidence.observation: finishDrag and cancelDrag are registered on window/document interruption paths and both clear dragRef, scenePanRef, guides and panning state.
evidence.effect: A drag no longer depends solely on SVG pointerup delivery for cleanup.

evidence.observation: Transform edits call clampLayerTransformValue; the main shell captures wheel events and releaseNumberInputWheel blurs only a focused number input.
evidence.effect: Sidebar scrolling cannot silently step a coordinate field, while keyboard and spinner editing remain available.

evidence.observation: Tests cover number-wheel eligibility, all four transform bounds and the four interruption-listener integrations.
evidence.effect: The identified accidental-move causes are directly protected from regression.

problems: No connected Chrome control extension was available for a live pointer-interruption reproduction, so the score remains below the 95-100 band.

checks_against.candidate: Rapid wheel events could repeatedly calculate from a stale render value and appear to bounce backward.
checks_against.result: Each event reads sceneZoomRef.current, immediately writes the new value back, and the listener no longer rebinds on each zoom render.

checks_against.candidate: A late IndexedDB recovery result could overwrite a zoom action performed immediately after page load.
checks_against.result: Pointer, keyboard and wheel interaction mark userInteractedRef; asynchronous recovery restores only when that flag is still false.

evidence.observation: sceneZoom synchronizes into a ref; the native non-passive Ctrl-wheel handler uses previous=sceneZoomRef.current and writes sceneZoomRef.current=next before scheduling state.
evidence.effect: Back-to-back events form one ordered sequence rather than restarting from the previous render.

evidence.observation: Keyboard, wheel and pointer interaction all set userInteractedRef, and recovery checks it before replacing history.
evidence.effect: Late recovery cannot revert a user-initiated zoom or edit.

evidence.observation: Tests cover 1.0→1.1→1.2→1.1 sequences, limits, cursor anchoring, ref writeback, recovery guard and preventDefault integration.
evidence.effect: Both the state-sequencing fix and original cursor-centered behavior have regression evidence.

checks_against.candidate: An oversized layer could be centered using its old size and then shrunk, leaving an incorrect edge position.
checks_against.result: The implementation normalizes width and height first, then calculates x and y from the normalized dimensions.

checks_against.candidate: Invalid or extreme transforms could produce NaN or positions beyond the Scene.
checks_against.result: Non-finite dimensions fall back to one pixel; dimensions are clamped to Scene bounds and centered coordinates are non-negative finite values.

evidence.observation: Width and height are finite-clamped to 1..scene dimension before x/y are derived from the remaining space.
evidence.effect: Normal and oversized objects use one deterministic center algorithm without order-dependent drift.

evidence.observation: The existing off-canvas recovery test remains, and a 1200×300 object in a 960×540 Scene is asserted as x=0, y=120, width=960, height=300.
evidence.effect: Both ordinary recovery and the previous oversized ordering gap are checked exactly.

scores.name: 大字級屬性面板版面

checks_against.candidate: The prior generic six-column selector could continue to squeeze distribution buttons and overlap the locate action.
checks_against.result: Dedicated higher-specificity classes set the alignment group to three columns, distribution to two columns with its own margin, and locate to a separate 40px-high row.

checks_against.candidate: Separating the layout could accidentally remove disabled conditions or click handlers.
checks_against.result: The JSX retains all six align handlers, both distribute handlers with selectedIds<3 disabled conditions, and the locateLayerInScene action.

evidence.observation: The panel contains m2-align-actions, m2-distribute-actions and a separate m6-locate button with original handlers and disabled logic intact.
evidence.effect: The three functional groups are structurally separable and retain behavior.

evidence.observation: Alignment uses three minmax columns, distribution uses two columns plus 8px top spacing, and locate has 40px minimum height plus 8px spacing and the 14px UI font level.
evidence.effect: The screenshot's six-column text collision and vertical overlap have bounded layout rules.

evidence.observation: Static integration tests require both row classes and their three/two-column grids.
evidence.effect: A return to the generic squeezed layout will fail the suite.

problems: A post-fix Chrome screenshot is unavailable because browser control is not connected; the score is capped within the 90-94 band rather than claiming direct visual observation.

checks_against.candidate: Global pointer and wheel guards could break canvas zoom, panning, Undo, export or performance.
checks_against.result: All 42 tests, PSD verification, lint and both performance cases pass, including existing drag threshold, two-axis pan, cursor anchor and export round-trip cases.

checks_against.candidate: Patch-version metadata could disagree between app assets and exported package manifests.
checks_against.result: package metadata, lockfile, project package toolVersion and cache-busted asset tests all target 0.19.1.

evidence.observation: Build, 42/42 tests, PSD validation, lint, 2/2 benchmark and diff checks are recorded as passing.
evidence.effect: The patch is supported by complete project-level checks, not only targeted unit tests.

evidence.observation: Legacy drag, two-axis pan, flow movement, Ctrl-wheel anchoring, flow-card dimensions and new interaction integrations remain asserted together.
evidence.effect: The requested fixes are checked alongside the features most likely to regress.
The changes form a traceable patch release.

summary: Round 1 internal audit finds all reported interaction and layout risks addressed with direct code and regression evidence. All criteria exceed 90; unavailable live Chrome evidence is explicitly reflected in C1 and C4 rather than assumed.
